turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Our baby's due in three weeks and I'm trying to fit the car seat. The instructions are a nightmare.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You're not alone, car seats are famously fiddly. Is it a base that clicks in, or does the seat use the car's seatbelt?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's a base with two metal arms.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Those usually slide into anchor points hidden in the gap of the back seat. Push the arms in until you hear a click and see green indicators.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Got the clicks. There's also a leg thing.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's the support leg. Lower it until it presses firmly on the floor, again you should see a green marker. Then try wiggling the base, it shouldn't move more than a little.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, rear facing for a baby, and never in front of an active airbag. Many fire stations or baby shops will check your installation for free if you want reassurance.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: me sleep a bit better, honestly.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Totally understandable. Good luck with the big arrival.
